title: PS 1 Part I Question 1
masterContent: Draw truth tables to solve the following problems.

parts.content: Prove that $\lor$ is *symmetric*. In other words, prove that if $P$ and $Q$ are propositions, then $P\lor Q\implies Q\lor P$.

responseInput.answer: {"question": "Draw truth tables to solve the following problems. Prove that $\\lor$ is \\emph{symmetric}. In other words, prove that if $P$ and $Q$ are propositions, then $P\\lor Q\\implies Q\\lor P$.", "answer": "We can just check all the cases. \\medskip \\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\\hline $P$&$Q$&$P\\lor Q$&$Q\\lor P$&$(P\\lor Q)\\implies(Q\\lor P)$\\\\ \\hline  {\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt false}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt true}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline \\end{tabular} \\medskip The fifth column is always {\\tt true}, hence $P\\lor Q\\implies Q\\lor P$ is always true."}

parts.content:
Is $\iff$ symmetric?
In other words, is it true that for all propositions $P$ and $Q$ we have
$(P\iff Q)\implies (Q\iff P)?$
Give a proof or a counterexample.

responseInput.answer: {"question": "Draw truth tables to solve the following problems. Is $\\iff$ symmetric? In other words, is it true that for all propositions~$P$ and~$Q$ we have $$(P\\iff Q)\\implies (Q\\iff P)?$$ Give a proof or a counterexample.", "answer": "It is symmetric, we can check all the cases. \\medskip \\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\\hline $P$&$Q$&$P\\iff Q$&$Q\\iff P$&$(P\\iff Q)\\implies(Q\\iff P)$\\\\ \\hline  {\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt false}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt true}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt false}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline {\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}&{\\tt true}\\\\ \\hline \\end{tabular} \\medskip The fifth column is always true so $(P\\iff Q)\\implies(Q\\iff P)$ is always true. Previous part questions that can be used without proof: a) Prove that $\\lor$ is \\emph{symmetric}. In other words, prove that if $P$ and $Q$ are propositions, then $P\\lor Q\\implies Q\\lor P$. b) Is $\\implies$ symmetric? In other words, is it true that for all propositions~$P$ and~$Q$ we have $$(P\\implies Q)\\implies (Q\\implies P)?$$ Give a proof or a counterexample. "}

parts.content:
Is $\implies$ symmetric? In other words, is it true that for all propositions $P$ and $Q$ we have
$(P\implies Q)\implies (Q\implies P)?$
Give a proof or a counterexample.

responseInput.answer: {"question": "Draw truth tables to solve the following problems. Is $\\implies$ symmetric? In other words, is it true that for all propositions~$P$ and~$Q$ we have $$(P\\implies Q)\\implies (Q\\implies P)?$$ Give a proof or a counterexample.", "answer": "It is not. For $\\implies$ to be symmetric, we must have $(P\\implies Q)\\implies(Q\\implies P)$ being true whatever $P$ and~$Q$ are. But if $P$ is false and $Q$ is true, then $P\\implies Q$ is true, $Q\\implies P$ is false, and $(P\\implies Q)\\implies(Q\\implies P)$ is then false. Previous part questions that can be used without proof: a) Prove that $\\lor$ is \\emph{symmetric}. In other words, prove that if $P$ and $Q$ are propositions, then $P\\lor Q\\implies Q\\lor P$. "}
